sections.title: Date and Time of Discharge
sections.promptHint: Doctor enters manually when starting the draft; DisDate in the system is empty until the hospital finalizes discharge.

sections.title: Diagnosis
sections.promptHint: List the primary diagnosis first, then secondary diagnoses. Use the exact clinical wording from the data; do not add or reclassify diagnoses.

sections.title: Presenting Complaints
sections.promptHint: Summarize distinct complaints of type 'Chief Complaint' only. Collapse repeated rows with the same complaint into one clean line, adding the recorded date or date range when useful. Do not include associated complaints or dump raw rows. Return one item per line; do not leave an escaped-newline marker visible in the text.

sections.title: History of Present Illness
sections.promptHint: Write a concise chronological History of Present Illness using the chief complaints plus associated complaints and their recorded remarks. Group repeated symptoms rather than listing every row. Return 2-4 useful lines separated by real line breaks, not a raw data dump. There is no dedicated HPI field, so use only this recorded proxy; do not invent detail or replace the narrative with a disclaimer. Add at most one short review caveat at the end if needed.

sections.title: Past Medical History
sections.promptHint: Summarize the distinct recorded problems as a concise Past Medical History. Include status and onset when recorded, one problem per line, and do not invent or reclassify conditions. Write the useful list first; add at most one short review caveat at the end if needed.

sections.title: Current Medication
sections.promptHint: List active medications using only the medication name, recorded schedule, start date, stop date, and route when recorded. Reconcile active orders with explicit note-recorded medications; note-only facts are provisional and require doctor verification. Use one medication per line, omit status, and do not invent dose or route.

sections.title: Personal History
sections.promptHint: No source in the API. Leave blank for the doctor; never invent habits, addictions, or lifestyle detail.

sections.title: Family History
sections.promptHint: No source in the API. Leave blank for the doctor; never invent family illness detail.

sections.title: Allergies
sections.promptHint: List each allergen with reaction nature and symptoms, or state the recorded status (e.g. NKA) if there are no items. Do not infer additional allergies.

sections.title: Occupational History
sections.promptHint: No source in the API. Leave blank for the doctor; never invent occupational detail.

sections.title: On Examination
sections.promptHint: Use the most recent vitals reading only. State explicitly that this covers recorded vitals, not a physical examination, and do not imply a fuller exam happened.

sections.title: Course in Hospital
sections.promptHint: Synthesize notes, lab orders, radiology orders, medication changes, and the vitals trend across the stay into 3-6 concise chronological lines separated by real line breaks. Do not reproduce raw lists or a medication list here; medication sections are canonical. Stick to what the data shows and make the result useful for a doctor reviewing the whole episode.

sections.title: Condition at Discharge
sections.promptHint: Base on the most recent vitals plus the current status of active problems. Do not overstate improvement; report the recorded values.

sections.title: Procedure
sections.promptHint: No procedures or OT record endpoint exists. Leave blank for the doctor; the generator must not write this section.

sections.title: Medications During Stay
sections.promptHint: List medication facts recorded during this episode, including explicit medications in clinical notes when no order exists. Use one line per medication with medication name, recorded schedule, start date, stop date, and route. Note-only facts require doctor verification; do not include raw JSON.

sections.title: Medications on Discharge
sections.promptHint: Draft a concise medication-on-discharge list using active discharge-suitable orders plus explicit active oral/topical medications recorded in notes. Exclude injections, IV/infusion/chemotherapy, inpatient-only supplies, and any medication not present in the reconciled facts. Note-only medications must remain visibly provisional for doctor verification. Use medication name, schedule, start date, and stop date; omit status and do not invent a replacement.

sections.title: Advice
sections.promptHint: Draft short patient-specific advice from explicit advice, restrictions, precautions, or instructions in progress/discharge notes. Use diagnoses only as context. If notes do not contain explicit advice, provide only a concise diagnosis-grounded draft for doctor review; do not invent doses, appointments, or restrictions.

sections.title: Special Needs
sections.promptHint: No source in the API. Leave blank for the doctor; never invent care needs.

sections.title: Follow Up Advice
sections.promptHint: Draft brief follow-up advice grounded primarily in the recorded diagnoses, using any explicit follow-up instructions in notes. Do not invent a clinic, interval, test, or treatment change that is not recorded; keep it useful and clearly for doctor review.
